body:
The problem is that Undertow doesn't challenge until setAuthenticationRequired is triggered.

But this is not triggered until there is a SecurityConstraint.

So I added this single line:

```java
        d.addSecurityConstraint(
                new SecurityConstraint().setEmptyRoleSemantic(SecurityInfo.EmptyRoleSemantic.AUTHENTICATE)
                        .addWebResourceCollection(new WebResourceCollection().addUrlPattern("/*")));

```
to "UndertowDeploymentTemplate" and now it works.

From my understanding of how it works, this mean that everyone must be authenticated so doesn't work for anonymous.

May be during template building can check given a property that tells what to do for empty roles, so that we can choose between PERMIT, DENY, AUTHENTICATE.

@starksm64 it does not look like we have any tests for basic auth? 

The issue here is that because the check is happening at the JAX-RS level it is already past the Undertow security layer. By default Undertow will attempt to authenticate via basic auth if the headers are present, however it will not issue a challenge unless it knows (generally via a security constraint) that auth is required.

I am not sure about the cleanest way to fix this, one way is to simply get hold of the current ServletRequestContext and call HttpServletRequest.authenticate().

Another more generic possibility might be to install an Undertow commit listener that checks for a 401 response and instead attempts to authenticate.

Other servers that use Undertow like Wildfly or Thorntail use the web.xml approach also for JAX-RS.

You put a constraint inside web.xml and the challenge start.

Do you think in Quarkus this approach cannot be used ?
